We know this is a valid block hash because the hash number 7657 is less than our target. Cool. We've got a few other things to validate before we consider the Genesis block valid. The next thing to verify is the coin-based transaction. Every block should have one. You can identify the coin-based transaction by the inputs field. It's the only transaction that will have no inputs. It's also always the first transaction in the block. Our validation worksheet says that we should check the total outputs in the coin base or less or equal to the block reward plus fees. There are no other transactions in the Genesis block, so we'll just have the block rewards in our coin-based transaction. For the first block, the coin-based reward is 50 bitcoin. We should check that the coin-based transaction doesn't have more than 50 bitcoins in its outputs. If you add up the output values, you should see that we have one output worth 25 bitcoin locked up to a green lock and three other outputs for the value of 8 bitcoins each. Adding these up, the total amount of outputs on our coin-based transaction is 49 bitcoins. This is less than 50 bitcoins, so this is a valid coin-based transaction.
